question_record.context: A user account, identified as `dp5hn` and possibly compromised, was observed delivering ransomware-related files such as `characterical.zip` and `characterical.zip.lockbit` on host `vnevado-win11t`. This incident was flagged on July 4, 2024, and indicated as part of a possible ransomware attack where an attacker might also be attempting lateral movement within the network.
question_record.question: What was the IP address used in the PsExec command to launch a remote device command as part of this incident?
solution: A ransomware-related file was dropped using the IP address `99.83.111.100`.
Lateral movement using PSExec was done to the host with AadDeviceId `4d8d23e9-a77d-4e33-9435-b8c457e57ca1`.
PSExec was used to launch a command on a remote device with IP address `107.224.99.179`.

93.name: Possible compromised user account delivering ransomware-related files
93.description: A user account was observed dropping a ransomware-related file on several devices. An attacker may have compromised the said user account to move laterally across the network and infect as many devices with ransomware as possible. Automated remediation action may be taken to disable the account.

84.name: PsExec launched a command on a remote device
84.description: PsExec was used to launch a command on a remote device. PsExec is a tool used to launch programs on remote, or local devices. An attacker might be leveraging this tool to launch malicious commands to a remote device and move laterally in the organization.
